players.product: 1.6T PAM4 DSP, TIAs, drivers, silicon photonics light engines, coherent DSP, custom XPU silicon

quarterly_data.signal: Record Q2 revenue of $2.739 billion, up 37% year-over-year and 13% sequentially, above the midpoint of guidance; data center revenue a record $2.17 billion (79% of total), up 18% sequentially and 46% year-over-year, accelerating from Q1 (+11% QoQ, +27% YoY)
quarterly_data.figure: $2.739B revenue; +37% YoY; +13% QoQ; $2.17B data center (79%); +46% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: Non-GAAP gross margin 58.9% (GAAP 53.1%); non-GAAP operating margin 36.6% (+180 bps YoY, +160 bps QoQ); non-GAAP EPS $0.94 (+40% YoY, a penny above guidance midpoint); GAAP EPS $0.33; operating cash flow $606 million, down slightly QoQ on higher capacity prepayments to suppliers
quarterly_data.figure: 58.9% non-GAAP gross margin; 36.6% non-GAAP operating margin; $0.94 non-GAAP EPS; $606M operating cash flow

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 FY2027 guidance: revenue $3.15 billion +/-5% (+15% QoQ, >50% YoY); data center revenue to grow more than 20% sequentially and roughly 75% year-over-year; non-GAAP gross margin 57.5%-58.5% (custom ramp is a sequential mix headwind); non-GAAP EPS $1.05-$1.15; Q4 expected to accelerate further both sequentially and year-over-year
quarterly_data.figure: $3.15B Q3 revenue guidance; +15% QoQ; >50% YoY; data center >20% QoQ / ~75% YoY; $1.05-$1.15 non-GAAP EPS

quarterly_data.signal: FY2027 revenue outlook raised to roughly $12 billion (~45% YoY growth) from ~$11.5 billion a quarter ago, with data center now expected to grow ~60% (from ~50%); FY2028 revenue outlook raised by $1.5 billion to ~$18 billion (~50% YoY growth, from ~45%), with data center growing more than 60% and custom more than doubling
quarterly_data.figure: ~$12B FY2027 revenue (~45% YoY); ~$18B FY2028 revenue (~50% YoY); data center +60% FY2027, >60% FY2028

quarterly_data.signal: Scale-out connectivity remains the largest growth driver: 800 gig optical DSP demand strong while 1.6T DSP business is ramping rapidly and expected to accelerate further in FY2028; scale-out switching on track to more than double this year on a strong 51.2T ramp across a broadening set of customers; TIA and driver demand continues to exceed expectations; optical DSPs, TIAs/drivers, DCI modules and scale-out switching are each on or ahead of the trajectory to a $1 billion annualized revenue run rate
quarterly_data.figure: 1.6T DSP ramping; scale-out switching >2x FY2027 on 51.2T; three connectivity lines each tracking to $1B annualized run rate

quarterly_data.signal: Scale-across: hyperscalers building AI clusters spanning multiple data centers; aggregate bandwidth for scale-across networks projected at more than 10x current front-end DCI networks; Marvell addresses it with coherent DSP-enabled 1.6T ZR and ZR+ DCI modules
quarterly_data.figure: >10x DCI bandwidth requirement; 1.6T ZR/ZR+ coherent DSP modules

quarterly_data.signal: Scale-up optics: customers initially deploy copper for scale-up but reach and bandwidth limits are driving them to optics and purpose-built UALink/ESUN/NVLink switches; customers are aggressively planning scale-up optics deployments starting as early as next year, evaluating NPO and CPO packaging with silicon photonics and three modulator technologies (MZM, EAM, MRM); Marvell sees strong NPO adoption at multiple customers alongside its CPO wins, and its FY2028 scale-up optics outlook has increased meaningfully versus the ~$300 million category outlook given last quarter (which included ~$150 million from the Celestial AI photonic fabric); scale-up optics and switching are the most meaningful part of the $1.5 billion FY2028 raise; NPO participation via SiGe TIAs/drivers plus the in-house light engine shown at OFC
quarterly_data.figure: scale-up optics FY2028 outlook up meaningfully vs ~$300M prior (Celestial AI CPO ~$150M); deployments as early as next year

quarterly_data.signal: Scale-up switching: Marvell supports all three purpose-built scale-up protocols via internally developed UAL and ESUN switches plus the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion partnership; engaged in multiple deep discussions with Tier 1 customers, each a multibillion-dollar lifetime revenue opportunity; Teralynx Ethernet switch franchise (from the 2021 Innovium acquisition) has expanded its customer base and 100T scale-out switches are also applicable to scale-up; optics attach expected to roughly double the switching SAM over the next few years
quarterly_data.figure: multibillion-dollar lifetime opportunity per Tier 1 scale-up switch engagement; optics attach ~2x switching SAM

quarterly_data.signal: Custom business: significant acceleration in the second half of FY2027; confident it will more than double year-over-year in FY2028 and accelerate significantly in FY2029, driven by both XPU and XPU-attach (CXL and custom NIC demand rising); progress on current and next-generation XPU programs at multiple hyperscalers; the other large new XPU program (analyst estimate $600-700 million next year) is tracking and part of the FY2028 doubling; $10 billion-plus FY2029 custom target now has upside bias
quarterly_data.figure: custom >2x YoY FY2028; >$10B FY2029 custom with upside

quarterly_data.signal: 8-K filed the week before the call: expanded commercial agreement and associated warrant with a key hyperscaler (one of the largest adopters of custom silicon; analysts identified it as Google and management confirmed Marvell is part of the TPU ecosystem) covering custom programs already in execution, new design wins and future programs; products attached to the TPU ecosystem include AI inference accelerators, storage controllers, network interface controllers, memory interface controllers and near-memory compute; revenue from covered programs through FY2028 already in the custom target, with the larger impact in FY2029 and beyond; an analyst cited $120 billion cumulative revenue over 6 years if all milestones are hit, which management did not dispute or size
quarterly_data.figure: analyst-cited $120B cumulative over 6 years at full performance; management not sizing until Investor Day

quarterly_data.signal: CXL / memory expansion (Structera): now deployed at multiple hyperscalers with varying architectures in extremely high volumes for inference memory expansion; memory scarcity is pushing customers to use more CXL; additional CXL design wins secured in the last couple of quarters
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure (extremely high volumes at multiple hyperscalers)

quarterly_data.signal: Supply: operations team securing additional capacity despite pervasive industry-wide constraints; on pace for approximately $1 billion of capacity prepayments to suppliers in FY2027, applied against future material purchases and funded from the balance sheet and operating cash flow

Communications and other end markets: Q2 revenue $568 million, down 3% sequentially and up 10% year-over-year; Q3 expected to decline in the low-to-mid teens percent both QoQ and YoY with a solid sequential recovery in Q4; FY2027 growth expected to approach the 10% target

Balance sheet: inventory $1.36 billion (down slightly QoQ); total debt $4.96 billion; gross debt/EBITDA 1.32x, net debt/EBITDA 0.27x; repurchased $200 million of stock and paid $54 million in dividends during the quarter; buybacks to continue to manage dilution
quarterly_data.figure: $1.36B inventory; $4.96B debt; 1.32x gross leverage; $200M buyback; $54M dividends

quarterly_data.signal: Operating model: FY2027 non-GAAP opex ~$2.55 billion (from $2.45 billion prior) with non-GAAP operating margin expected to enter the 38%-40% long-term target range in Q4 FY2027; FY2028 opex to grow at roughly half the rate of revenue, reaching the upper end of the 38%-40% range through the year; FY2028 gross margins expected in a similar range to the back half of FY2027; non-GAAP tax rate ~13% in FY2028; long-term model to be reset at the Investor Day
quarterly_data.figure: ~$2.55B FY2027 non-GAAP opex; 38%-40% operating margin range from Q4 FY2027

quarterly_data.signal: Investor Day in New York City on October 6, 2026: deeper dive on long-term growth drivers, custom revenue trajectory through the end of the decade, memory expansion (CXL) section, and a reset of the long-term operating model

Management transitions: Willem Meintjes stepped down as CFO in mid-June, succeeded by former board member Dan Durn; Ashish Saran to retire from IR in April 2027, succeeded by Ross Seymore (formerly Deutsche Bank semiconductor analyst)
